summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with HLA-B27-positive ankylosing spondylitis and a history of chronic pain, was admitted for severe upper and mid-back pain radiating to the anterior chest wall, along with new left hip pain, lasting six and two days respectively. The pain was exacerbated by movement and limited his ability to breathe deeply. He had recently tapered his oral Dilaudid from every four to every six hours and transitioned from sertraline to Cymbalta. Evaluation revealed no infection, fracture, or cardiopulmonary pathology. Elevated CRP of 18.1 supported an inflammatory flare of ankylosing spondylitis. He was stabilized on Dilaudid 8mg every four hours, acetaminophen, lidocaine cream, and increased Cymbalta to 30mg twice daily. The chronic pain service performed trigger point injections, which improved his symptoms. He was discharged home with continued pain medications, a plan for weekly PCP follow-up, and a scheduled pain clinic visit to establish a multimodal pain management strategy including interventional procedures, pain psychiatry, and social work support.
